name: Major cyber incidents
summary: CISA listed five exploited flaws on 17–18 Nov; bank vendor breaches disclosed 19 Nov; no national-scale attack
state: CISA added five actively exploited vulnerabilities on 17–18 Nov, in Puppet Enterprise, Synology DiskStation Manager, BerriAI LiteLLM, REDCap and Apache Axis (CISA). JPMorgan Chase and Mastercard said on 19 Nov that third-party vendors were hacked, exposing some customer names or emails, with no service disruption (ABC13). Coles said on 16 Nov it is investigating a cyber incident; stores were unaffected (BleepingComputer). Continued exploitation of widely used products keeps Watch.
for_you: Organisations running the affected products should follow CISA and NCSC patching guidance. Customers of affected banks should be alert to phishing emails using their name; the NCSC gives advice on spotting scams.
rubric_hit: Mass-exploited vulnerabilities in widely used products (Watch): 5 CISA KEV additions 17–18 Nov; no national-scale attack

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
